hook: They were told to lick the glowing paint. It was poison.
narration: They were told to lick the glowing paint. It was poison. In the 1910s, young women in American factories painted watch dials with a miracle substance called radium. It made the numbers glow in the dark. Their bosses told them to point the brushes with their lips. They were told it was harmless. Some of the women even painted their nails and teeth for fun, and laughed when they glowed in the dark. Then their teeth began to fall out. Their jaws crumbled. Doctors had no answer, and the companies blamed disease. But the women refused to stay quiet. They took the companies to court, and they changed the law. Today, workers have safety rules because they spoke up. When someone tells you something is safe, ask who benefits from your silence.
title: They were told to lick the glowing paint. It was poison.
